status: proposed 2026-10-05; changes published scores, so it waits for Max's ruling (cos decision). decided_on is the draft date; a release sets it to the ruling's date.
basis: policybench/reference_exclusions.py: an output is excluded for every model when its reference depends on an engine input the prompt never listed and a careful reader could take the stated facts the other way.

exclusions.alternative_reading: The prompt lists no state income tax withheld or paid during 2026. The reference fills the state income tax part of the federal state and local tax deduction (26 U.S.C. 164(a)(3), (b)(5)) with policyengine-us's formula estimate of California income tax withheld: California's single rate schedule applied to the person's whole federal AGI (including $17,624.75 of taxable Social Security, which California exempts) less California's single standard deduction, at California's 2025 amounts (ca_withheld_income_tax, under the c_ca_hold_2025 convention), $6,058.85. The same engine computes the household's California income tax before refundable credits as $2,505.87. Read as the household paying its 2026 California income tax during the year, the deduction takes that liability and the output is the alternative value. The prompt's rule that unlisted numeric inputs are 0 gives a third reading, no state income tax paid, under which SALT takes the general sales tax (the note gives that value).
exclusions.unlisted_input: state income tax withheld or paid during 2026, which the federal state and local tax deduction takes as its state income tax part; policyengine-us fills it with state_withheld_income_tax, a formula estimate on federal AGI that the household data never set
exclusions.note: Found 2026-10-05 by sweeping every reference with the state income tax in SALT read three ways (reference_audit/2026-10-05/scripts/sweep_salt_withholding.py, on policyengine-us 2.15.17 with latest_final; its baseline reproduces all 1,928 scored references, and an independent re-implementation agreed on all 1,984 outputs). SALT is $14,887.85 in the reference and $11,334.87 under the alternative; the household itemizes under both, and the $40,400 cap binds under neither. Under the zero reading SALT takes the general sales tax, $1,155.60, and the output is $12,192.29; that sales tax includes the engine's local component of $192.60 (20% of the state table amount, an estimate for an unlisted locality), and without it the output is $12,234.66. The alternative uses the engine's California liability ($2,505.87), which this household's state output carries as an engine-defect exclusion; with the corrected liability ($1,968.81, recorded on policyengine-us 1.755.4) the output is $12,013.38. The output also moves under an engine defect: policyengine-us 2.15.17 leaves the household's California SDI contributions ($684.26) out of SALT, though they are deductible state income taxes (Trujillo v. Commissioner, 68 T.C. 670 (1977)). With them the output is $10,963.04 under the withholding estimate and $11,744.69 under the liability.

already_excluded.existing_basis: whether the prior-year deduction of the refunded state and local tax reduced federal tax (prior-year itemization, the income-versus-sales-tax election, SALT-cap headroom)
already_excluded.note_to_append: The output also moves under the state income tax withheld reading (unlisted input): the reference's SALT uses the Maryland withholding estimate ($15,791.66); with the engine's own liability ($11,295.39) the 2.15.17 value is $24,799.16, and with no state income tax paid it is $27,290.70. The $40,400 cap that binds in the reference does not bind under the liability, so the liability value depends on the county, which the prompt does not state: $24,705.95 to $25,068.44 across Maryland's 24 county rates (the engine's default, Allegany, gives $24,799.16).

The output also moves under the state income tax withheld reading (unlisted input): the reference's SALT uses the Connecticut withholding estimate ($12,010.05); with the engine's own liability ($11,917.18) the 2.15.17 value is $40,438.95, and with no state income tax paid it is $43,619.93. With r02's IRA fix on 2.15.17 the value is $40,423.18 under the withholding estimate, $40,445.46 under the liability and $43,629.21 with no state income tax paid. policyengine-us 2.15.17 also leaves the household's Connecticut paid leave contributions ($827.98) out of SALT (Rev. Rul. 2025-4); with them the 2.15.17 value is $40,217.95.
